name: Touching the Cloud
summary: In an HMD, the user's tracked bare hands appear in the point cloud; points are marked by touching them with a fingertip within a tolerance radius, then set as selected or unselected by voice or button.
howItWorks: Hands are tracked by a depth camera on a tripod, and the cloud sits above a virtual table. A two-hand pinch rotates, scales and translates the cloud so small parts can be reached. Touching points with a fingertip marks those within a customisable radius; marked points can then be added to or removed from the selection. The finished selection is annotated by saying a label after the keyword 'annotate', and an exploded copy of it allows hierarchical annotation. Two people tried it informally.
advantages: Natural direct touch with bare hands.
limitations: Hand-tracking jitter and depth misjudgement make fingertip touch imprecise.

relationships.note: Fingertip touch with a tolerance radius.
